plan: My private value is $27. In a second-price sealed bid auction, optimal strategy is typically to bid close to my true value. Since I want to maximize potential profit, I'll bid slightly above my value to increase winning chances. The worst case is bidding too high and losing money. A bid around $30 balances potential gain and risk, giving me buffer above my true value while not overcommitting.

My value is $31. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is to bid my true value. If I bid less, I risk losing the item even when winning would be profitable. If I bid more, I risk paying more than the item is worth to me. The worst case is paying close to my value, but bidding $31 ensures I only win if the prize is genuinely worth more than the second-highest bid. This maximizes my expected profit.

My private value is $20. In a second-price auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. If I bid less, I risk losing the item when my value exceeds my bid. If I bid more than my true value, I risk paying more than the item is worth to me. The worst case is paying close to my true value and not winning. Therefore, I will bid my exact private value of $20.
